checklist.description: Establish the navigation contract: the cause is that independent Skill and Site entry points are grouped inside Controls. The browser shell owns their placement and shared dropdown behavior; settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js already own their lists and actions. Preserve those owners and existing application capabilities. Update the checkout's navigation, Skills, and Knowledge Hub intent docs to describe the requested arrangement.

Update src/surfaces/web/static/index.html so the right-aligned actions appear in order: Skills, Sites, Settings, New Goal. Move the existing Skill and Site containers into their respective dropdowns. Rename the Controls button and accessible label to Settings. Reuse shared summary, panel, icon, and menu-row styles from css/base.css; preserve the remaining settings controls and New Goal's related creation actions.

Update settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js to show existing entries followed by a separator and an action group: New Skill then Manage Skills, or New Site then Manage Sites. New actions open the existing creation modals; management links navigate to #/settings/skills and #/settings/knowledge-hub. Keep these actions available with empty lists, and render list failures separately from the action group. Preserve Skill eligibility, input preflight, agent-tab launch, and Site draft/published URL handling.

Bind each list's refresh-on-open listener to its new dropdown while retaining existing load, definition-change, and node-context refresh behavior and stale-response guards. Use common.js's shared topbar menu handling for mutual exclusion, action dismissal, outside clicks, and Escape. Extend shared selectors only where needed. Use shared border and spacing tokens for separators, and verify panels remain usable with long lists and narrow viewports.

Update user-facing navigation references in Guide, Skill help, reporter onboarding, and toolbar Todo copy to the new locations. Preserve existing route and element identities where practical, including Node and Reporter selectors, so the label change does not break shell integrations.

Update src/surfaces/web_server/tests/static_surface/navigation.rs and add focused browser coverage for action order, exclusive list placement, separators, all four create/manage actions, empty and failed lists, refresh after node or definition changes, Skill launch, and Site opening. Exercise keyboard operation, dismissal, light/dark themes, and desktop/narrow layouts. skill.name: Plan
skill.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For behavior changes, identify the underlying cause, governing concept or invariant, and existing owner before listing edits. Prefer strengthening an existing concept; introduce one only when it clarifies the behavior and reduces special cases. Do not change repository files. 

### Guidance

- Thrashing is a real danger with AI agents. To mitigate this, consider if the Goal is merely a symptom of a missing or misused concept in the target app architecture. Feel free to explore other Goals to determine if they have additional insights into this question.
- Over- or under-specificity can also cause undesirable implementation outcomes. Ensure that the plan has the information it needs for effective implementation, but not unnecessary details.
- Always use plain language.

### Format

Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

Example:
Task #1 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
Task #2 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
(etc.)

### Intent and architecture

Review Refine's relevant documentation files under Refine's runtime at `<refine-runtime>/docs/intent/***/*.*` as the durable product specification.
